claims.claim: Randall counts that only three chapters of the Fionavar Tapestry are focalized through a single character while chapter 8 of The Summer Tree shifts focalization twenty-one times in twenty-four pages, which he reads as strategy rather than ineptness.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings

claims.claim: Randall counts twenty-six distinct focalizants in the trilogy plus, in a very few places, an unspecified omniscient focalizant.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: employs twenty-six different agents of focalization (focalizants)

claims.claim: Randall places Kay's multi-focalized technique with the richly populated Victorian novel and the thick historical novel of Dorothy Dunnett rather than with single-focalizer fantasies like Tolkien, Donaldson or Wolfe.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: closest correlation is to the thick historical novel

claims.claim: Randall argues the shifts (1) let the reader assimilate the secondary world, (2) build knowledge of character, (3) move the story from kernel to kernel, and (4) delay the unfolding of each plot-line, all serving a rhetoric of grandeur and scope.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: the shifts delay the unfolding of the story

claims.claim: Randall shows Darien's climactic line being deferred: his maturation is postponed by six other kernels across sixty pages, and during his search for Rakoth the narrative shifts focalization eighty-seven times with Darien as focalizant only nine.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: shifts focalization eighty-seven times, with Darien as focalizant only nine

claims.feature: register contrast: plain vs high style
claims.claim: Randall contrasts Darien's death (short sentences, concrete description, matter-of-fact tone, strictly focalized) with the zero-focalized 'high style' of the Arthurian departure, arguing the register tracks who is perceiving.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: Sentences are short, description is concrete.

claims.claim: Randall notes that Kevin's death, Paul's death on the Summer Tree, Diarmuid's death and the Arthurian departure are written as an obvious attempt at rhetorical high style, i.e. myth-in-the-making passages.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings

claims.claim: Randall reads the Darien plot as carried by a rhetoric of the sentimental, with attempts at child-like thought and pathos in both the classical and common senses.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: contains a rhetoric of the sentimental

claims.claim: Randall documents the trilogy's hierarchy of Book > Chapter > Section (marked by a graphic symbol from the jacket painting) > Subsection (marked by blank space), the units within which focalization shifts occur.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: Sections are distinguished by a graphic symbol

claims.claim: Randall contrasts Kay with Tolkien's off-stage Aragorn: Kay keeps important events from surprising the reader by shifting attention among characters far more frequently.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: determined not to have important events surprise us

claims.claim: Randall identifies the few zero-focalized (omniscient) passages as the mythic set pieces perceived by no character, e.g. the Arthurian trio's departure.
claims.source: Neil Randall, 'Shifting Focalization and the Strategy of Delay: The Narrative Weaving of The Fionavar Tapestry', Canadian Literature 129 (Summer 1991), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: shifts to an unspecified focalizant, to omniscience

claims.claim: Kleander's count: twenty-one focalizants and more than 150 focalizations in Tigana, Devin focalized forty-one times, Dianora twenty-seven, plus twenty-one separate non-focalized passages.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)
claims.quote: twenty-one separate focalizants in Tigana, and more than 150 separate focalizations

claims.claim: Kleander shows Part One's twenty-two focalizations (twelve through Devin) uphold a simple good/evil quest before Part Two hands nine of twelve sections to Dianora and demolishes the image of Brandin as evil.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)
claims.quote: made up of twenty-two separate focalizations

claims.claim: Kleander notes Brandin, who originates the whole fabula, is focalized through only once, for about a page at the end of the battle, after the reader has already formed a judgment.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)
claims.quote: No more than a page long, Brandin’s focalization

claims.claim: Kleander quotes Kay that the prologue of Sailing to Sarantium was written as a mosaic of different focalizations.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)
claims.quote: the prologue of Sailing to Sarantium was written as a mosaic

verdicts.trueWording: Only three chapters ... focalized through just one character
verdicts.note: Raw page: 'Only three chapters in the entire trilogy are focalized through just one character, and one chapter, the eighth of The Summer Tree, shifts focalization twenty-one times. Obviously, shifting the focalization twenty-one times in twenty-four pages demonstrates either ineptness or strategy on the part of the author, and ineptness can be ruled out on two major grounds.' Every limb (three single-focalized chapters, ch.8 of The Summer Tree, 21 shifts, 24 pages, strategy-not-ineptness) is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: employs twenty-six different agents of focalization (focalizants)
verdicts.note: Raw page: 'The Fionavar Tapestry employs twenty-six different agents of focalization (focalizants) and even adds, in a very few places, an unspecified omniscient focalizant.' Quote verbatim; both limbs (26 focalizants; the very-few-places omniscient focalizant) present.

verdicts.trueWording: owes much more to the richly populated Victorian novel
verdicts.note: Raw page: 'But Kay's work owes much more to the richly populated Victorian novel than to the sparser contemporary novel; in fact, its closest correlation is to the thick historical novel of the Dorothy Dunnett tradition.' The contrast class is Tolkien/Donaldson/Wolfe/Kinsella. Precision note for re-use: Randall's wording is 'the four fantasies mentioned above are focalized through one or two central characters' - not 'single-focalizer'. Do not re-quote him as saying single.

Raw page lists all four: assimilate the world of Fionavar; 'they form our knowledge of character'; 'the constant shifting moves the novel from incident to incident, and in fact makes possible the co-ordination of important events (kernels in Barthes' terminology)'; 'the shifts delay the unfolding of the story'; closing with 'all four point as well towards a rhetorical effect of grandeur and scope.' Third effect is worded 'incident to incident' with kernels glossed in the same sentence; 'kernel to kernel' is Randall's own later phrase ('The shifts in focalization move the plot from kernel to kernel').

verdicts.trueWording: delayed by a succession of no fewer than half a dozen other significant kernels
verdicts.note: Raw page: 'sixty pages of narrative have transpired' before the maturation scene, with six intervening kernels enumerated (Arthur/Cavall, Jennifer as Guinevere, Kim and the Baelrath, the boar hunt, Diarmuid's proposal, Kevin's sacrifice) and summarised as 'no fewer than half a dozen other significant kernels'; and 'During Darien's search for Rakoth, the narrative shifts focalization eighty-seven times, with Darien as focalizant only nine of those times, usually in brief passages.' All limbs on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: Sentences are short, description is concrete.
verdicts.note: Raw page, on Darien's death: 'Sentences are short, description is concrete. Except for the first two and the last sentences, the scene is restricted to Darien's sensory perception. The tone, moreover, is matter-of-fact.' On the Arthurian departure: 'the language here is an obvious attempt at rhetorical "high style"' and 'The difference lies in the focalization ... The departure of the trio is more magnificent because it is perceived by minds capable of comprehending magnificence.' Register-tracks-perceiver limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: an obvious attempt at rhetorical “high style.”
verdicts.note: Raw page: 'Like the language of many other passages in the Tapestry (cf. Kevin's death, Paul's death on the Summer Tree, Diarmuid's death), the language here is an obvious attempt at rhetorical "high style." It represents, of course, myth in the making'. All four passages named; myth-in-the-making limb explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: contains a rhetoric of the sentimental
verdicts.note: Raw page: 'This passage, like most of the Darien plot, contains a rhetoric of the sentimental, with the narrative concentrating almost solely on pathos' and 'the attempt at child-like thought is obvious'. The classical/common split is stated earlier of Darien's fall: 'pathetic in both the classically rhetorical sense (the appeal to the emotions) and the more commonly used sense (pity for a seemingly small action)'.

verdicts.trueWording: Books are divided into Chapters, Chapters into Sections, and Sections into Subsections
verdicts.note: Raw page footnote 2: 'a part of the chapter separated by a graphic symbol taken from the painting on the jacket ... Books and Chapters are numbered, Sections are distinguished by a graphic symbol, and Subsections are prefaced by a blank space on the page.' The last limb is supported by the main text: 'sections separating most of the shifts and with only occasional shifts without an accompanying section or sub-section break' - i.e. Randall's frame is that sections/subsections SEPARATE the shifts.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay seems determined not to have important events surprise us in this way
verdicts.note: Raw page, after the Aragorn / Pelennor Fields example: 'Kay seems determined not to have important events surprise us in this way; he arranges the story's kernels in a more tightly-knit fashion than does Tolkien, mainly through a much more frequent shifting of our attention from one character to another.' Note Randall hedges with 'seems determined'; the claim states it flatly.

verdicts.trueWording: perceived by minds capable of comprehending magnificence
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim: 'The departure of the Arthurian trio is one of several brief passages in the trilogy that shifts to an unspecified focalizant, to omniscience, to what Genette calls zero focalization'. But the page says the OPPOSITE of 'perceived by no character' for this passage - 'The departure of the trio is more magnificent because it is perceived by minds capable of comprehending magnificence' (and the text itself: 'it seemed to those that watched from the plain'). 'because in his case there are no observers' is said of Darien's death, which is strictly focalized, NOT zero-focalized. The 'mythic set pieces' limb is also weakened: Randall says the departure 'represents, of course, myth in the making, but for Fionavar the incident is less mythically significant than Darien's death.' Zero focalization means an UNSPECIFIED focalizant, not an unperceived event.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that the zero-focalized passages are perceived by no character

verdicts.trueWording: twenty-one separate focalizants in Tigana, and more than 150 separate focalizations
verdicts.note: Raw page, footnote 1: 'In addition to the non-focalized narrative, there are twenty-one separate focalizants in Tigana, and more than 150 separate focalizations. Devin is focalized through forty-one times, and Dianora twenty-seven times. There are twenty-one separate occasions of non-focalized narrative, excluding short passages with zero focalization within focalized sections.' All five figures match. The 21 non-focalized occasions EXCLUDE short zero-focalized passages inside focalized sections - carry that qualifier if the figure is re-used.

verdicts.trueWording: She is the focalizant of nine of the twelve sections of Part Two
verdicts.note: Raw page: 'Part One, that is the first 150 pages of the novel, is made up of twenty-two separate focalizations: Devin is the focalizant for twelve of these'; 'those focalizations all uphold the uncomplicated story of a peninsula taken over by Brandin and Aberico, the malevolent tyrants, and the resistance against these' (and 'the lines between good and evil are clearly drawn'); 'She is the focalizant of nine of the twelve sections of Part Two'; 'This complex emotional response of a major focalizant demolishes the previous image of Brandin as evil'. Every limb present.

verdicts.trueWording: he is central to all the story kernels ... and the originator of the fabula
verdicts.note: Raw page: 'Returning to Brandin, he is central to all the story kernels of Tigana, and the originator of the fabula. Yet, Brandin is only focalized through at the very end of the battle ... By this point, the readers have had time to assimilate all the information given about the Sorcerer King and thus had the chance to form their own opinion about him before Kay reveals what Brandin thinks of himself. No more than a page long, Brandin's focalization is one of the most powerful sections of the story.' Kleander's wording is 'had the chance to form their own opinion', slightly weaker than 'has already formed a judgment'.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay is quoted only for ‘written as a mosaic’
verdicts.note: Raw page: "Kay's novels heavily rely on this technique, for example 'the prologue of Sailing to Sarantium was written as a mosaic' (Kay in New York Review of Science Fiction Interview 2000, url) of different focalizations." The quotation marks CLOSE after 'a mosaic' and the citation follows; 'of different focalizations' is Kleander's own completion of her sentence, not part of what she quotes from Kay. Kleander does assert the mosaic is of focalizations, but Kay must not be re-quoted as having said 'a mosaic of different focalizations'.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that Kay's quoted words include 'of different focalizations'
